title: Conjecture
body_md: Let $X$ be a graph, and let $H$ be a finite graph. Then $X$ has no $K$-fat $H$ minor for some $K \in \mathbb{N}$ if and only if $X$ is $f(K)$-quasi-isometric to a graph with no $H$-minor, where $f : \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ depends on $H$ only.
head: environment

label: quest:add
title: Question
body_md:
\label{quest:add}
	For which finite graphs $H$ it is true that if a graph $X$ has no $K$-fat $H$-minor for some $K \in \mathbb{N}$, then $X$ admits a map of bounded additive distortion onto a graph with no $H$ minor?
head: environment

label: quest:K_2t
title: Question
body_md:
\label{quest:K_2t}
	Is it true that if a graph $X$ has no $K$-fat $K_{2,t}$-minor for some $K \in \mathbb{N}, t\geq 3$, then $X$ admits a map of bounded additive distortion onto a graph with no $K_{2,t}$-minor?
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md: Let $H$, $G$ be graphs, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be an honest, $R$-bounded $H$-partition of $G$ for some $R \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $G$ is $(R + 1, R/(R + 1))$-quasi-isometric	to $H$.
head: environment

label: thm:additive
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:additive}
	For $k\geq 1, R\geq 1$, let $G,H$ be two graphs such that $sipco\left(G\right)\leq k, sipco\left(\langle H \rangle\right)\leq k$, and $G$ admits an honest, nicely rooted $R$-bounded $H$-partition.  There is a graph $F$ with $tw(F) \leq tw(H)$  and $G$ admits a $(1,33\cdot R \cdot k^2)$-quasi-isometry to $F$.
head: environment

label: thm:K2t
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:K2t}
There is a function $g:\mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ such that for any graph $G$ without any $K$-fat $K_{2,t}$-minor for $t\geq 3$, there is a $K_{2,t}$-minor-free graph to which $G$ admits a $(1,g(K,t))$-quasi-isometry.
head: environment

label: def:asym
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:asym}
	A graph class $\cal G$ contains $H$ as an \emph{asymptotic minor} if for every integer $K\geq 1$, there exists a graph $G\in \cal G$, such that $G$ contains $H$ as a $K$-fat minor.
head: environment

label: def:quasi
title: Definition
head: environment

label: def:add
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:add}
	A class $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs admits a \emph{quasi-isometry with additive distortion} to a class $\mathcal{H}$ if there exists a constant $A$  (depending only on $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{H}$) such that any $G\in \mathcal{G}$ admits a $(1,A)$-quasi-isometry to a graph in $\mathcal{H}$.
head: environment

label: lem part QI
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem part QI}
	Let $H, G$ be graphs, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be an honest, $R$-bounded $H$-partition  of $G$ for some $R\in \mathbb{R}$. Then $G$ is $(R + 1, R/(R+1))$-quasi-isometric to~$H$.
head: environment

label: def:nice
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:nice}
	For an integer $R$, let $\mathcal{H}= (H, (V_h)_{h \in V(H)})$ be an $R$-bounded honest graph partition of a graph~$G$ over a graph~$H$ which is also rooted at a node $s$. We say $\mathcal{H}$ is ``\emph{nicely rooted}'' if 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),noitemsep,topsep=0pt]
		\item\label{it:independent} for all $j\in \mathbb{N}$, the layer $L^j$ is an independent set,
		
		\item\label{it:level} there exists a vertex $r\in V_s$ such that $V_s=B_G(r,R_s)$ with $R_s\le R$, and for every node $h\neq s$, $V_h$ is level,
		
		\item\label{it:same-height} the heights of two nodes $ x,y\in V(H)$ lying in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ are the same. 
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:down-bd-dst
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:down-bd-dst}
	For an integer $R$, let $\mathcal{H}= (H, (V_h)_{h \in V(H)})$ be an $R$-bounded nicely rooted honest graph-partition of a graph~$G$ over a graph~$H$ which is also rooted at a node $s$. Let $r\in V_s$ be a vertex such that $V_s=B_G(r,R_s)$. Let $g$ and $h$ be two nodes of $H$ that lie in the same cluster of $H$ w.r.t $s$. For any $w\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{h}, x\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{g}$, $d_{G}\left(r,w\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,x\right) $. Moreover, for any $y\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{h}, z\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g}$, $d_{G}\left(r,y\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,z\right) $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the lemma by induction on the layer that contains $g$ and $h$. Assume $g,h\in L^1$. For two vertices $w\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{g}, x\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{h}$, there exist $w',x'\in V_s$ such that $\{ww',xx'\}\subseteq E(G)$. 
	By Definition~\ref{def:nice}\ref{it:level}, $d_{G}\left(r,w'\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,x'\right) =R_s$.  Hence, $d_{G}\left(r,w\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,w'\right) +1 = R_s+1$ and $d_{G}\left(r,x\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,x'\right) +1 = R_s+1$. Hence, $d_{G}\left(r,w\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,x\right) $. 
	Suppose $y\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g},z\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{h}$. As any $(r,y)$-isometric path contains a vertex of $\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}$ and by the above arguments, all vertices of $\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}$ are equidistant from $r$ in $G$, it follows that $d_{G}\left(r,y\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}\right)  + R_g$. Similarly,  $d_{G}\left(r,z\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{h}\right)  + R_h$. 
	Since $g$ and $h$ lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$, $R_h=R_g$ (due to Definition~\ref{def:nice}\ref{it:same-height}). By the above arguments $d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{h}\right)  = R_s+1$. Hence,   $d_{G}\left(r,y\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,z\right)  = R_s+1+R_h$.   
	
	For an integer $k\geq 1$, assume the statement is true for all pairs of nodes that lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ and lie in $L^i$ with $i\leq k$. Now consider two nodes $g$ and $h$ that lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ and $g,h\in L^{k+1}$. Let $w\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{g},x\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{h}$ and let $g',h'\in L^k$ be nodes such that there exist $w'\in V_{g'}, x'\in V_{h'}$ with $ww'\in E(G)$ and $xx'\in E(G)$. Observe that, $g'$ and $h'$ lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ and $w'\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g'}, x'\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{h'}$. Hence, $d_{G}\left(r,w'\right) =d_{G}\left(r,x'\right) $. Since $d_{G}\left(r,w\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,w'\right) +1$ and $d_{G}\left(r,x\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,x'\right) +1$, we have that $d_{G}\left(r,w\right) =d_{G}\left(r,x\right) $. 
	
	For the second part, consider two vertices $y\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g}, z\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{h}$. As any $(r,y)$-isometric path contains a vertex of $\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}$ and by the above arguments, all vertices of $\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}$ are equidistant from $r$ in $G$, it follows that $d_{G}\left(r,y\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}\right)  + R_g$. Similarly,  $d_{G}\left(r,z\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{h}\right)  + R_h$. 
	Since $g$ and $h$ lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$, $R_h=R_g$ (due to Definition~\ref{def:nice}\ref{it:same-height}) and $d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{g}\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,\delta^{\downarrow}_{h}\right) $.
head: environment

label: lem:dst-incerase
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dst-incerase}
	For an integer $R$, let $\mathcal{H}= (H, (V_h)_{h \in V(H)})$ be an $R$-bounded nicely rooted honest graph-partition of a graph~$G$ over a graph~$H$ which is also rooted at a node $s$. Let $r\in V_s$ be a vertex such that $V_s=B_G(r,R_s)$. For $gh\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$ and $u \in V_g, v\in V_h$, $d_{G}\left(r,u\right)  < d_{G}\left(r,v\right) $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $P$ be an $(r,v)$-isometric path in $G$. 
	Let $X=\displaystyle\bigcup\limits_{g'\in L^{\ell_{g}}} \delta^{\uparrow}_{g'}$ and by definition (of nicely rooted graph partitions), $X$ is an $(r,v)$-separator in $G$. 
	Hence, there exists a node $g'$ in $L^{\ell_{g}}$ such that $P$ contains a vertex $w_1\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g'}$. Observe that $d_{G}\left(r,v\right)  > d_{G}\left(r,w_1\right) $. Moreover,  $g,g'$ lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ in $H$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:down-bd-dst}, for a vertex $w_2 \in \delta^{\uparrow}_{g}$, $d_{G}\left(r,w_1\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,w_2\right) $. Now observe that $d_{G}\left(r,u\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(r,w_2\right)  = d_{G}\left(r,w_1\right)  < d_{G}\left(r,v\right) $.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: For an integer $R$, let $\mathcal{H}= (H, (V_h)_{h \in V(H)})$ be an $R$-bounded honest graph partition of a graph $G$ over a graph $H$. For $u,v\in V(G)$ and a $(u,v)$-isometric path $P$ in $G$, $trace_{H}\left(P\right)$ is a sequence  $\left(g_1,g_2,\ldots,g_k\right)$ of distinct elements such that for $i\in [k], g_i\in V(H)$, $u\in V_{g_1}, v\in V_{g_k}$, and for $i\in [k-1]$, there is an edge $e_i=u_iv_i\in E(G)$ such that $u_i\in V_{g_i}\cap V(P), v_i\in V_{g_{i+1}}\cap V(P)$.
head: environment

label: lem:trace
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First we prove \ref{it:trace}. Let $P$ be an $(r,u)$-isometric path in $G$. We prove that
 		for any node $a\in V(H)$, $V_a\cap V(P)$ induces a subpath of $P$. 
 	
 		To prove the above claim, suppose there exists a node $a\in V(H)$ such that the graph $F$ induced by $V_a\cap V(P)$ has at least two components. For distinct connected components $C,C'$ of $F$, let $P(C,C')$ be the minimal subpath of $P$ that has vertices adjacent to both $C$ and $C'$. 
 		Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be two components of $F$ such that none of the vertices of $P(C_1,C_2)$ lie in $V_a$. 
 		Without loss of generality, assume the vertices of $C_1$ are closer to $r$ in $G$ than those of $C_2$. 
 		In other words, for $u\in V(C_1), v\in V(C_2)$, $d_{G}\left(r,u\right) <d_{G}\left(r,v\right) $. Let $Q=P(C_1,C_2)$. For $i\in \{1,2\}$, let 
 		$f_i=u_iv_i\in E(G)$ such that $u_i\in V(C_i)$ and $v_i\in V(Q)$.  Observe that $d_{G}\left(r,u_1\right)  < d_{G}\left(r,w\right) $ for all $w\in V(Q)$. 
 		
 		If $v_1$ lies in a node $b\in V(H)$ where $\ell_{b}=\ell_{a}-1$, then by Lemma~\ref{lem:dst-incerase}, $d_{G}\left(r,v_1\right)  < d_{G}\left(r,u_1\right) $, which is a contradiction. Hence, $v_1$ lies in a node $b\in V(H)$ where $\ell_{b}=\ell_{a}+1$. Observe that $u_1\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{a}$.
 		Let $w\in V(Q)$ be the vertex which is closest to $u_1$ in $G$ and is adjacent to some vertex $w_1$ where $w_1\in V_{c}\setminus \{u_1\}, c\in L^{\ell_{a}}$. 
 		Since $Q$ is a connected  subgraph which has vertices adjacent to both $C_1$ and $C_2$,  $w$ always exists. Observe that $w_1\in \delta^{\uparrow}_{c}$. 
 		Moreover, $a$ and $c$ lie in the same cluster w.r.t $s$ in $H$. Hence, by Lemma~\ref{lem:dst-incerase} and Lemma~\ref{lem:down-bd-dst}, $d_{G}\left(r,u_1\right) =d_{G}\left(r,w_1\right) $, which is a contradiction. 
 
 	\medskip\noindent Let $trace_{H}\left(P\right)=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k)$. Since for $i\in [k]$, $V_{a_i}\cap V(P)$ induces a subpath of $P$,  observe that, for $j\in [2,k]$, $a_j$ is the unique node of $H$ that contains the endpoint of the path induced by $V(P)\setminus \{V_{a_1}\cup \ldots \cup V_{a_{j-1}}\}$ which is also adjacent to a vertex of $V_{a_{j-1}}$. Next,  we prove that 
 		for $j\in [k-1]$,  $d_{H}\left(s,a_{j+1}\right)  = d_{H}\left(s,a_j\right) +1$. 
 
 	 To prove the above claim, suppose for some $j\in [k-1]$, $d_{H}\left(s,a_{j+1}\right) \leq d_{H}\left(s,a_j\right) $. Let $w_1w_2\in E(P)$ be the unique edge such that $w_1\in V_{a_j}\cap V(P)$ and $w_2\in V_{a_{j+1}}\cap V(P)$. Clearly, $d_{H}\left(s,a_{j+1}\right) =d_{H}\left(s,a_{j}\right) -1$ and $d_{G}\left(r,w_1\right)  < d_{G}\left(r,w_2\right)  $. But this contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:dst-incerase}. 
 	Hence, $trace_{H}\left(P\right)$ is an $(s,h)$-isometric path.
 	
 	\medskip \noindent To prove \ref{it:rooted-pair-preserve}, let $P$ be an $(r,y)$-isometric path in $G$ that contains $x$. By \ref{it:trace}, $Q=trace_{H}\left(P\right)$ is an $(s,h)$-isometric path in $H$. Since $x\in V(P)$, $g\in V(Q)$. Hence $(g,h)$ is an $s$-rooted pair in $H$.
head: environment

label: def:strong
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:strong}
	The ``\emph{strong isometric path complexity}'' of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $sipco\left(G\right)$, is the minimum integer $k$ such that for every vertex $r\in V(G)$, $ipco\left(r,G\right)\leq k$.
head: environment

label: th:sipco-K_2,t
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:sipco-K_2,t}
	The strong isometric path complexity of graphs that do not contain $K_{2,t}$ as a $K$-fat minor is at most $(48K+5)t-1$.
head: environment

label: lem:sipco-distort
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $P$ be any $(u,v)$-isometric path in $X$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ be a minimum cardinality set of $r$-rooted isometric paths in $X$ that covers $P$ and for any $Q\in \mathcal{Q}$, $|V(P)\cap V(Q)|$ is maximized. Let $z\coloneq |\mathcal{Q}|$ and by definition, $z\leq sipco\left(X\right)$. Observe that for any $Q\in \mathcal{Q}$, the path induced by  $V(P)\cap V(Q)$ is an isometric path in $X$.  Moreover, there exists exactly one path $Q_1\in \mathcal{Q}$ that contains $u$. Otherwise, if there exists a path $Q'\in \mathcal{Q}\setminus \{Q_1\}$ containing $u$, then either $V(P)\cap V(Q')$ contains $V(P)\cap V(Q_1)$, or vice versa.  But this contradicts the minimality of $\mathcal{Q}$.
	
	Let $Q_1\in \mathcal{Q}$ be the path containing $u$, and define $P_1\coloneq P[V(P)\cap V(Q_1)]$. 
	Let $a_1\coloneq u$, and $b_1$ be the end-vertex of $P_1$ distinct from $a_1$, unless $P_1$ is reduced to a single vertex in which case $b_1=a_1$.  
	
	For $i\in\{2,\ldots, z\}$, let $Q_i\in \mathcal{Q}$ be a path that contains the end-vertex of the path induced by $V(P)\setminus \displaystyle\bigcup\limits_{j<i} V(Q_j)$ which is distinct from $v$. For $i\in\{2,\ldots, z\}$, let $P_i= P[V(P)\cap V(Q_i)]$, and $a_i$ be the end-vertex of $P_i$ which is adjacent to $b_{i-1}$ in $P$, and let $b_i$ be the end-vertex of $P_i$ distinct from $a_i$. Note that $b_z=v$.
	Hence,
	
	\begin{equation*} \label{eq1}
		\begin{split}
			d_{Y}\left(f(u),f(v)\right)  & = d_{Y}\left(f(a_1),f(b_z)\right)  \\
			& \leq \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z} d_{Y}\left(f(a_i),f(b_i)\right)  + \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z-1} d_{Y}\left(f(b_i),f(a_{i+1})\right) \\
			& \leq \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z} (d_{X}\left(a_i,b_i\right) +t) + \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z-1} (k+1) \hspace{10pt} \\
			& \leq   \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z} d_{X}\left(a_i,b_i\right)  + \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^{z-1} d_{X}\left(b_i,a_{i+1}\right) + t\cdot z + k(z-1) \\
			& \leq  d_{X}\left(a_1,b_z\right)  + t\cdot z + k(z-1) \\
			& =   d_{X}\left(u,v\right)  + t\cdot z + k(z-1)
		\end{split}
	\end{equation*}
	This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:attach-ipco
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:attach-ipco}
Let $H$ be a graph such that $sipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)\leq k$. Then, for any path $P$ of $H$ and a component $C$ of $H-V(P)$, $|N_H(C)\cap V(P)|\leq k$.
head: environment

title: Proof

label: clm:W
title: Claim
body_md:
\label{clm:W}
		The path $P$ is isometric in $H^*$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: y definition, $P$ is a path in $H^*$.  Let $x,y$ be the endpoints of $P$ and $Q$ be any $(x,y)$-path distinct from $P$. By definition of $H^*$, $Q$ must contain a subpath of length at least $t_1+2$ and hence $|E(Q)|>|E(P)|$.
head: environment
name: B

label: clm:ipcok+1
title: Claim
body_md:
\label{clm:ipcok+1}
	Any $r$-rooted isometric path in $H^*$ contains at most one vertex of $N_H(C)\cap V(P)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: y construction of $H^*$, for any $u\in N_H(C)\cap V(P)$, $d_{H^*}\left(r,u\right) = t_3$. (Indeed,  for any $u\in N_H(C)\cap V(P)$, there is an $(r,u)$-path in $H^*$ through $r_u$ that has length $t_3$ and any other $(r,u)$-path will have length at least $t_4>t_3$.) Hence, any path of $H^*$ that has $r$ as an endpoint and contains two vertices of $N_H(C)\cap V(P)$ will have length at least $t_3+1$, and thus not isometric in $H^*$.

name: B

label: lem:sipco-F
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sipco-F}
	Treewidth of $F$ is at most that of $H$ and $sipco\left(F\right)\leq sipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)+2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For every node $g$ and vertex $v\in V_g\setminus \{r_g\}$, delete from $F$, all vertices of $Q_v\setminus \{r_{p(g)}\}$. The resulting graph, say $F^*$, is a subdivision of $H$. Since subdivision of edges preserves treewidth, we have that $tw(F)\leq tw(H)$.
	 For the second part, let $k=sipco\left(\langle H\rangle \right)$ and $P$ be any isometric path of $F$. Let $E_1$ be the set of edges of  $P$ that lie in some pendant path of $F$. Clearly $E_1$ induces at most two components $C_1,C_2$ and $E(P)\setminus E_1$ induces an isometric path $Q$ of $F^*$.	Let $v$ be any vertex of $F$. 
	
	Suppose $v\in V(F^*)$. Since $F^*\in \langle H \rangle$, $sipco\left(F^*\right)\leq k$ i.e. vertices of $Q$ can be covered with at most $k$ many $v$-rooted isometric paths in $F^*$, and thus in $F$. Since $C_1,C_2$ are subpaths of pendant paths, each of them can be covered with one $v$-rooted isometric path in $F$. Therefore, $P$ can be covered with $k+2$ many $v$-rooted isometric paths. 
	
	Suppose $v\not\in V(F^*)$. If $v$ is incident to some edge in $C_1$ or $C_2$, then $P$ can be covered with two $v$-rooted paths. Otherwise,  there exists a vertex $v'\in F^*$ such that any isometric path in $F$ containing $v$ as an endpoint also contains $v'$. Since $F^*\in \langle H \rangle$, $sipco\left(F^*\right)\leq k$,  similar arguments as above imply that $P$ can be covered with $k+2$ many $v$-rooted paths.
head: environment

label: dist:rep
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{dist:rep}
	The graph $F$ satisfies the following. 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),topsep=0pt]
		\item\label{it:dr1} For an edge $e=gh\in E(H)   $ with $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$, $d_{G}\left(r_g,r_h\right) \leq 2R+1$, the length of $P_e$ is at most $2R+1$, and
		 $d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  \leq 2R+1$.
		
		\item\label{it:dr2} For a node $h\in V(H)$, and a vertex $v\in V_h\setminus \{r_h\}$, the length of $Q_v$ is at most $3R+1$ and, $d_{F}\left(v,r_{p(h)}\right) \leq3R+1$.
		
		\item\label{it:dr4} For any $v\in V(G), h\in V(H)$ with $v\in V_{h}$, $d_{F}\left(v,r_h\right)  \leq 5R+2$.
		
		\item\label{it:dr5} For an edge $uv\in E(G)$, $d_{F}\left(u,v\right)  \leq 12R+5$.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To prove \ref{it:dr1}, assume without loss of generality $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$. By definition, $r_h$ is a vertex of $\delta^{\downarrow}_{h}$ and there exists $x\in V_g, x'\in \delta^{\downarrow}_{h}$ such that $xx'\in E(G)$. Since $d_{G}\left(x,r_g\right) \leq R$ and $d_{G}\left(x',r_h\right) \leq R$, we have $d_{G}\left(r,r_h\right)  - d_{G}\left(r,r_g\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(r_h,r_g\right) \leq 2R+1$.  Now the statement follows from the definition of $P_e$ and the definition of $F$.

\medskip \noindent To prove \ref{it:dr2}, observe that  $d_{G}\left(v,r_{p(h)}\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(v,r_{h}\right)  +  d_{G}\left(r_{h},r_{p(h)}\right) $. By definition, $d_{G}\left(v,r_{h}\right)  \leq R $. Now \ref{it:dr1} implies $ d_{G}\left(r,v\right)  - d_{G}\left(r,r_{p(h)}\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(v,r_{p(h)}\right)  \leq 3R+1$. Now the statement \ref{it:dr2} follows from the definition of $Q_v$, and the definition of $F$. 


  
	\medskip \noindent	To prove \ref{it:dr4}, observe that $d_{F}\left(v,r_h\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(v,r_{p(h)}\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_h,r_{p(h)}\right) $. Now \ref{it:dr1} and \ref{it:dr2} imply $d_{F}\left(v,r_h\right)  \leq 5R+2$. 
	
	\medskip \noindent	To prove \ref{it:dr5}, consider an edge $xy\in E(G)$. First assume there exists a vertex $h\in V(H)$ such that $x,y\in V_h$.
	Observe that $d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(x,r_h\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_h,y\right) $. By \ref{it:dr4}, $d_{F}\left(x,y\right) \leq 10R+4$. 
	Now consider the case when there is an edge $e=gh\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$ and $x\in V_h, y\in V_g$. Observe that $d_{F}\left(x,y\right) \leq d_{F}\left(x,r_h\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_h,r_g\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_g,y\right) $. Now \ref{it:dr1} and \ref{it:dr4} imply, $d_{F}\left(x,y\right) \leq 12R+5$.

label: lem:no-increase
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:no-increase}
	For any $s$-rooted pair $(g,h)$ in $H$, $d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(r_g,r_h\right) $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $g=h$, the lemma is trivially true. So, assume $g\neq h$ and let $(g,h)$  be an $s$-rooted pair in $H$ and $P$ be any $(s,h)$-isometric path in $H$ that contains $g$. Let $e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_k$ be the edges of the $(g,h)$-subpath of $P$ where $e_1$ is incident to $g$, for $i\in [k-1]$, $e_i,e_{i+1}$ share an endpoint and $e_k$ is incident to $h$. For $i\in [k]$, let $e_i=g_ih_i$ such that $d_{H}\left(s,g_i\right) =d_{H}\left(s,h_i\right) -1$. Observe that, $g=g_1, h=h_k$, and $i\in [k-1]$, $h_i=g_{i+1}$. Thus,
	\begin{align*}
		d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  & \leq \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^k d_{F}\left(r_{g_i},r_{h_i}\right) \\
		& \leq \displaystyle\sum\limits_{i=1}^k d_{G}\left(r,r_{h_i}\right)  - d_{G}\left(r,r_{g_i}\right)  & [\text{Definition of }F]\\
		& = d_{G}\left(r,r_{h_k}\right)  - d_{G}\left(r,r_{g_1}\right) \\
		& \leq d_{G}\left(r_{h},r_g\right) 
	\end{align*}
	This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:G->F
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:G->F}
	There is a function $\beta\colon V(G)\rightarrow V(F)$, such that all of the following hold. 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),topsep=0pt]
		\item\label{it:distG-1} For each $x\in V(F)$, there is a vertex $y\in V(G)$ such that $d_{F}\left(x,\beta(y)\right)  \leq 3R+1$. 
		
		\item\label{it:distG-2} For each edge $xy\in E(G)$, $d_{F}\left(\beta(x),\beta(y)\right)  \leq 12R+5$. 
		
		\item\label{it:distG-3} For any $r$-rooted pair $(x,y)$ in $G$, $d_{F}\left(\beta(x),\beta(y)\right)  \leq d_{G}\left(x,y\right)  + 12R+4$.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition, any vertex of $G$ is also a vertex of $F$. For $x\in V(G)$, define $\beta(x)=x$. Hence for $x,y\in V(G)$,  $d_{F}\left(\beta(x),\beta(y)\right) =d_{F}\left(x,y\right) $. 
	
	
	\medskip \noindent To prove \ref{it:distG-1}, any vertex of $F$ is contained in some path in $\mathcal{S}$, 
	and that the endpoints of the paths in $F$ are identified with vertices of $V(G)$. Now  \ref{it:distG-1} follows from Lemma~\ref{dist:rep}\ref{it:dr1} and \ref{it:dr2}. 
	
	\medskip \noindent Statement \ref{it:distG-2} follows from Lemma~\ref{dist:rep}\ref{it:dr5}.
	
	\medskip\noindent To prove \ref{it:distG-3}, consider two vertices $x,y\in V(G)$ such that there is an $(r,y)$-isometric path in $G$ that contains $x$. Let $g,h\in V(H)$ be the vertices of $H$ such that $x\in V_g$ and $y\in V_h.$
	If $g=h,$ then $d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(x,r_g\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_g,y\right) $. 
	Lemma~\ref{dist:rep}\ref{it:dr4} implies $d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  \leq 10R+4$. Otherwise, $g\neq h$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:trace}\ref{it:rooted-pair-preserve}, there is a $(s,h)$-isometric path in $H$ that contains $g$ i.e. $(g,h)$ is an $s$-rooted pair in $H$.  Therefore, \begin{align*}
		d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  &  \leq	d_{F}\left(x,r_g\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  + d_{F}\left(r_h,y\right)  \\
		& \leq 	10R+4 + d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  & [\text{Lemma~\ref{dist:rep}\ref{it:dr4}}] \\ 
		& \leq 10R+4 + d_{G}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  & [\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:no-increase}}]\\
		& \leq  10R+4 + d_{G}\left(r_g,x\right)  + d_{G}\left(x,y\right)  + d_{G}\left(y,r_h\right)  \\ 
		& \leq 12R+4 + d_{G}\left(x,y\right)  & [V_g,V_h~\text{have diameter at most }R ]
	\end{align*}
	This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:equal-GF-rooted
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:equal-GF-rooted}
	Let	$(g,h)$ be an $s$-rooted pair in $H$ such that $(r_g,r_h)$ is an $r$-rooted pair in $G$. Then, $d_{G}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  = d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right) $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The case $g=h$ is trivial, and hence assume $g\neq h$. Let $P$ be an $(r_g,r_h)$-isometric path in $F$, and let
	$r_{g_1},r_{g_2},\ldots,r_{g_k}$ be the ordering of the representative vertices encountered on $P$ when traversed from $g_1=g$ to $g_k=h$.
	By the construction of $F$,
	\[
	|E(P_{e_i})|
	=d_G(r,r_{g_{i+1}})-d_G(r,r_{g_i}).
	\]
	Therefore,
	\begin{align*}
		d_F(r_g,r_h)=|E(P)|	& =\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}|E(P_{e_i})|\\
		&=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}
		d_G(r,r_{g_{i+1}})-d_G(r,r_{g_i}) \\
		&=d_G(r,r_h)-d_G(r,r_g)\\
		&=d_G(r_g,r_h),
	\end{align*}
	where the last equality holds because $(r_g,r_h)$ is an
	$r$-rooted pair in $G$.
	Together with Lemma \ref{lem:no-increase}, we have the proof.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rooted-rep-F-dist}
	Let $g,h\in V(H)$ be two nodes such that $(r_g,r_h)$ is an $r$-rooted pair in $F$. Then, $d_{G}\left(r_g,r_h\right) \leq d_{F}\left(r_g,r_h\right)  + 2R\cdot sipco\left(\langle H \rangle\right)$.

name: F

label: lem:F->G
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The function $\alpha\colon V(F)\rightarrow V(G)$ is defined as follows. 
Let $x\in V(F)$ be a vertex. If $x$ is also a vertex of $G$, then define $\alpha(x)=x$. 
Otherwise, if there exist $y\in V(G), h\in V(H)$ such that $y\in V_h\setminus \{r_h\}, x\in V(Q_y)$ where $Q_y\in \mathcal{S}$, then define $\alpha(x)=r_{p(h)}$. 
Otherwise there exists $e=gh\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$ and $x\in V(P_e)$ where $P_e\in \mathcal{S}$. In this case define $\alpha(x)=r_g$. This concludes the definition of $\alpha$.

Using $\alpha$, we define a function $\alpha'\colon  \mathcal{S}\rightarrow 2^{V(G)}$ as follows. Let $Q\in \mathcal{S}$ be a path. 
Assume for some $e'=gh\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g}=\ell_{h}-1$, $Q=P_{e'}$. Define $\alpha'(Q)=\{r_g,r_h\}$.
Now assume for some $z\in V(G)$ and $h'\in V(H)$, $Q=Q_z$ and $z\in V_{h'}$.  In this case, define $\alpha'(Q)=\{z,r_{p(h')}\}$.
By Lemma~\ref{dist:rep}\ref{it:dr1} and \ref{it:dr2}, for any $Q\in \mathcal{S}$ and $\{a,b\}=\alpha'(Q)$, $d_{G}\left(a,b\right) \leq 3R+1$.  


\medskip \noindent To prove $(a)$, let $e=xy$ be any edge of $F$.  Observe that there exists a path $T_e\in \mathcal{S}$ such that $e\in E(T_e)$.  By definition, $\{\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\}\subseteq \alpha'(T_e)$. 
The above arguments imply, $d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right) \leq 3R+1$.  

\medskip \noindent To prove $(b)$, let $x,y\in V(F)$ such that there is an $(r,y)$-isometric path $Q$ in $F$ that contains $x$.  If $x=y$, then the lemma is trivially true.
For \(x\ne y\), let \(e_x\) be the edge immediately after \(x\) toward \(y\) along \(Q\), and \(e_y\) be the edge immediately before \(y\). Let $T_x,T_y\in \mathcal{S}$ be two paths containing $e_x$ and $e_y$, respectively.
 If $T_x=T_y$, then $\{\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\}\subseteq \alpha'(T_x)$ and thus $d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right) \leq 3R+1$.  
 Assume $T_x\neq T_y$. Then there exists $e_1=g_1h_1\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g_1}=\ell_{h_1}-1$ such that $P_{e_1}=T_x$. By definition, $\alpha(x)\in \{r_{g_1}, r_{h_1}\}$. 
 
 
\medskip \noindent \textbf{Case 1.} Suppose there exists $e_2=g_2h_2\in E(H)$ with $\ell_{g_2}=\ell_{h_2}-1$ such that $P_{e_2}=T_y$. Then $\alpha(y)\in \{r_{g_2},r_{h_2}\}$. 
Since $T_x\neq T_y$, $Q$ contains $r_{g_1}, x, r_{h_1}, r_{g_2},y$. 
This implies $Q$ contains $\alpha(x),x,\alpha(y),y$ and $d_{F}\left(r,\alpha(x)\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,x\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,\alpha(y)\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,y\right) $. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
	d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right)  & \leq d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right)  + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right) & [\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:rooted-rep-F-dist}}] \\
	& =  d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),x\right)  +  d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  - d_{F}\left(\alpha(y),y\right)  + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right) \\ 
	& \leq 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)  + 2R + 1 + d_{F}\left(x,y\right) .
\end{align*}
 
 \medskip \noindent \textbf{Case 2.} Suppose there exists $h_2\in V(H)$, and $z\in V_{h_2}\setminus \{r_{h_2}\}$ such that $Q_{z}=T_y$. Then $\alpha(y)\in \{y,r_{p(h_2)}\}$. 
 Since $T_x\neq T_y$, and $Q$  contains $r_{g_1}, x, r_{h_1}, r_{p(h_2)},y$ and $d_{F}\left(r,r_{g_1}\right) \leq d_{F}\left(r,x\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,r_{h_1}\right) \leq d_{F}\left(r,r_{p(h_2)}\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,y\right) $. 
 This implies $Q$ contains $\alpha(x),x,\alpha(y),y$ and $d_{F}\left(r,\alpha(x)\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,x\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,\alpha(y)\right)  \leq d_{F}\left(r,y\right) $.  
If $\alpha(y)=r_{p(h_2)}$ then, 
 \begin{align*}
 	d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right)  & \leq  d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right)  + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)  & [\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:rooted-rep-F-dist}}] \\
 	& =  d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),x\right)  +  d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  - d_{F}\left(\alpha(y),y\right) +2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)  \\ 
 	& \leq 2R + 1 + d_{F}\left(x,y\right) +2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right) .
 \end{align*}
 Otherwise, $\alpha(y)=y$ and thus,    \begin{align*}
 	d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)\right)  &  \leq	d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),r_{p(h_2)}\right)  + d_{G}\left(r_{p(h_2)},y\right)  \\
 	& \leq 	d_{G}\left(\alpha(x),r_{p(h_2)}\right)  + 2R+1 \\ 
 	& \leq d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),r_{p({h_2})}\right)  + 2R+1 + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)  \hspace{1cm} [\text{Lemma~\ref{lem:rooted-rep-F-dist}}]\\
 	& =  d_{F}\left(\alpha(x),x\right)  +  d_{F}\left(x,y\right)  - d_{F}\left(r_{p({h_2})},y\right)  + 2R+1 + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right)  \\ 
 	& \leq 4R + 2 + 2R\cdotsipco\left(\langle H\rangle\right) + d_{F}\left(x,y\right) .
 \end{align*}
This completes the proof.

label: cor:subdivision
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:subdivision}
		For $k\geq 1, R\geq 1$, let $G,H$ be two graphs such that $sipco\left(G\right)\leq k, sipco\left(\langle H \rangle\right)\leq k$, and $G$ admits an honest, nicely rooted $R$-bounded $H$-partition.  There is a graph $F$ that has $H$ as a core and $G$ admits a $(1,33\cdot R \cdot k^2)$-quasi-isometry to $F$.

label: lem:albr
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:albr}
	There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ such that for any graph $G$ without any $K$-fat $K_{2,t}$-minor, there is an honest, nicely rooted $f(K,t)$-bounded $H$-partition of $G$ where $H$ is $\Theta_t$ minor-free.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~3.4 of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding} with $3K.$ Since $G$ contains no $K$-fat $K_{2,t}$-minor, Lemma~2.1 of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding} implies that $G$ contains no $3K$-fat $\Theta_t$-minor. Hence, Lemma~3.4 of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding} provides an honest, $R(t,3K)$-bounded $H$-partition satisfying properties (i)-(iv) of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding}. 

    We root $H$ at the node $s$ used in the construction of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding}. Property~\ref{it:independent} of our Definition~\ref{def:nice} is exactly (i) of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding}. Property~\ref{it:level} follows from (ii) of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding} : the root class is a ball around the distinguished root vertex, while every other class is level.

    It remains to check \ref{it:same-height}, consider two nodes $h_A,h_B\in L^{n+1}$ that belong to the same cluster with respect to $s.$ By the construction provided by Lemma~3.4 of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding}, the partition $\mathcal{P}$ is the union of the partitions $\mathcal{P}_D,$ where $\mathcal{D}$ ranges over the classes of the partition $\mathcal R$ of the components of $G-G^n.$ Moreover, for every component $C\in \mathcal{P}_D,$ the height $R_C$ of $C$ depends on the component $D$ such that $C\in \mathcal{P}_D.$ Thus, it is enough to prove $A$ and $B$ belong to $\mathcal{P}_D$ for the same $D\in \mathcal{R}.$ 

    Suppose, for a contradiction, that $D_A\neq D_B.$ Recall that $h_A,h_B\in L^{n+1}.$ If at least one of $D_A,D_B$ is a singleton $\{C\},$ then, by the definition of $\mathcal{R},$ $C$ has neighbors in exactly one partition class $V_x$ for some vertex $x\in L^n.$ In this case, one of $V_{h_A}, V_{h_B}$ is contained in $C$, and $V_x$ separates $V_{h_A}$ from $V_{h_B}$ in $G.$ Consequently, every path between $h_A$ and $h_B$ in $H$ contains $x,$ and hence $h_A$ and $h_B$ lie in distinct components of $H-B_H(s,n)$.   
    
    Otherwise, both $D_A$ and $D_B$ are of the form $D_Z$ for some components $Z$ of $G-G_{n-1}.$ Since $D_A\neq D_B,$ the corresponding components $Z_A$ and $Z_B$ are distinct. Moreover, $V_{h_A}\subseteq Z_A$ and $V_{h_B}\subseteq Z_B.$ Hence any path in $H$ between $h_A$ and $h_B$ must contain a node of $L^n,$ otherwise, by the definition of an $H$-partition, the corresponding bags would yield a path in $G-G_{n-1}$ joining $Z_A$ and $Z_B,$ a contradiction. Thus again $h_A$ and $h_B$ lie in distinct components of $H-B_H(s,n).$

    In both cases, $h_A$ and $h_B$ cannot belong to the same cluster with respect to $s$, since they both lie in $L^{n+1}.$ This contradiction shows that $D_A=D_B.$ Therefore                             
    $$R_{h_A}=R_A=R_B=R_{h_B},$$
    Hence, \ref{it:same-height} follows.

    Finally, if $H$ contained $\Theta_t$ as a minor, then, since $\Theta_t$ is $2$-connected, Lemma~3.3 of \cite{albrechtsen2025excluding} would yield a $3K$-fat $\Theta_t$-minor in $G,$ a contradiction. Thus $H$ is $\Theta_t$-minor-free. Taking $f(K,t)=R(t,3K)$ proves the lemma.
